feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no result is stated for it. The candidate is the iteration 5 design (best raced score 175.70: kp 3.0, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.6, outer sensors at x = ±0.04, sensor_size 0.016, last_direction) with one change: ki from 0.4 to 0.8. The values are inside the contract limits, and the change is a clean single-variable test. Iteration 5 showed that kd 0.5 raised progress on the bends (s-bend 0.17 to 0.40) at the cost of oval finish rate (0.25 to 0.05). Iteration 1 showed that low rms_error (0.023 to 0.027) and low steering oscillation (0.15 to 0.33) are consistent with a steady offset that integral action could remove. ki has not been tested alone, so this is the right next lever. Earlier races rejected wider outer sensors (iteration 3, 54.87) and higher kp (iteration 4, 108.24), so do not change those. After the race, compare against 175.70 and check four things per track: progress on s-bend and slalom, max_error, steering_oscillation, and oval finish rate. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.35, integral windup or noise is the likely cause, so return ki to 0.4 (iteration 5 value). If the score is at or above 175.70 with progress unchanged or higher, keep ki 0.8 and consider a further single step such as ki 1.0. If the score falls below 175.70 with progress unchanged, keep iteration 5 as the fallback.
requested_changes: After the race, if steering_oscillation on the oval or s-bend exceeds about 0.35, return ki to 0.4 and keep kd 0.5, since iteration 5 showed oscillation at 0.33 is close to the limit and extra integral gain adds to it.

If the score rises above 175.70 with progress on s-bend and slalom at or above iteration 5 levels (0.40 and 0.12), test ki 1.0 with all other fields unchanged, to see whether the residual steady offset keeps shrinking.
Do not change sensor positions, kp, or base_speed in this step. Iterations 2, 3 and 4 each showed those moves lowered the score relative to the best design.
